title.narrative: Strengthening Inclusive Partnerships for Smallholders in Rain-fed Areas (SIPRA)

description.narrative: EMM will engage specifically with The Challenge Fund, aimed at promoting inclusive business partnerships is designed and disseminated with clear and tailored targets, and project staff duly trained and prepared to monitor its performance

Population of targeted localities is 1.6 million, direct target group is 120,000 people (24,000 producer households). The project will be implemented in Central Darfur (Gharb Jabal Marrah [Nertiti], Wasat Jabal Marrah [Golo], Shamal Jabal Marrah [Rokoro], Zalingi and Umm Dukhun), in East Darfur (Abu Karinka, Adila, Ad Du’ayn rural), in South Darfur (Mershing, Beliel and Al Sunta) and in South Kordofan (Kadugli, Ar Reif Ash Shargi, Al Quoz)

The Strengthening Inclusive Partnerships for Smallholders in Rain-fed Areas (SIPRA) project will bring about transformative change for smallholders in West Sudan. It will establish inclusive partnership modalities between organised producers (with sustained increased income and selling capacities) and a motivated private sector with fair modalities for engaging with producer groups, focusing on empowered women and youth. Through strengthened agro-SMEs sourced by large agri-businesses, investors and sellers’ reach will sustainably be linked to smallholder producers. An enabling business and policy environment will continually be fostered through advocacy and engagement with key stakeholders and knowledge institutions on barriers impacting actors in the value chain. Driving the programme is the food systems approach and market-driven strategies which will select value chains that are in sustainably high demand, and ideally linked to export markets (such as oil seeds, gum arabic and livestock etc). The project will reach an estimated 2,460,000 individuals, and directly target 132,000 individuals (22,000 households, a realistic reach for the type of targeted interventions required).
